investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to go unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible regardless of capacity, and the 2 eligible nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" with no preemption victims available. Because no pod can be placed, no VM is provisioned, and the eval probe times out (~146 s) without ever writing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those nodes, leaving none available for new probe pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules. If node labels were recently changed or nodes were replaced without the required labels, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk, accelerating resource exhaustion on the remaining 2 nodes.

Less likely — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents workload: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote agent pods than is currently being requested (by the eval probes plus any real workloads), causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

Least likely — eval runner submitting pods with overly restrictive affinity selectors: if the affinity rules in the pod spec were recently tightened (e.g., requiring a label present on fewer nodes), the schedulable pool would shrink. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this hypothesis at this time.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-create probe that produces a pod in Running state and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would disprove that the resource is exhausted.

kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the affinity-eligible nodes would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and shift focus to a different scheduling or API failure.

A scheduler message citing a different reason (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota, network policy) rather than 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' in a re-run would indicate the root cause is different from resource exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod affinity selector was recently changed to exclude more nodes (e.g., a Kubernetes manifest diff) without a corresponding node label update would shift the primary cause to affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of remote-agent-create concurrent with a failing run of an unrelated check would confirm the issue is isolated to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool and not a broader cluster or API outage.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes and warns before exhaustion occurs, rather than only detecting it after a pod fails to schedule.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote agent VMs or pods are left in a running or pending state after the remote-agent probe suite completes, catching resource leaks before they cause scheduling failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider adding a latency-to-schedulable metric to the remote-agent-create probe that records how long the pod spent in Pending state before becoming Running, enabling trend detection of capacity pressure before full exhaustion.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-21T12:24–12:29Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on its 2 peer-pod-capable nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new remote-agent pod. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot; that call timed out after ~143–147 seconds, leaving the evidence object empty and triggering the contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No agent pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote agent pods, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the VM-backed peer-pod resource slots are fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every eval attempt that calls createAgent with type "remote" times out waiting for a schedulable pod (~143–152 seconds), and the eval runner records a failure with empty evidence before the expected-output contract can be satisfied. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to these observability evals.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and all contract assertions to go unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible regardless of capacity, and the 2 eligible nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" with no preemption victims available. Because no pod can be placed, no VM is provisioned, and the eval probe times out (~146 s) without ever writing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before any agent was created.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message at endedAt=2026-06-21T12:29:08.361Z, ~5 minutes after the first failure, confirming no recovery occurred during the observation window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; the scheduler rejection prevents this call from completing, so no evidence is ever written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated because the evidence object is empty.
possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those nodes, leaving none available for new probe pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules. If node labels were recently changed or nodes were replaced without the required labels, the effective scheduling pool may have shrunk, accelerating resource exhaustion on the remaining 2 nodes.

Less likely — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents workload: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote agent pods than is currently being requested (by the eval probes plus any real workloads), causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

Least likely — eval runner submitting pods with overly restrictive affinity selectors: if the affinity rules in the pod spec were recently tightened (e.g., requiring a label present on fewer nodes), the schedulable pool would shrink. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this hypothesis at this time.

Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible by node affinity/selector for remote agent pods, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the VM-backed peer-pod resource slots are fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every eval attempt that calls createAgent with type "remote" times out waiting for a schedulable pod (~143–152 seconds), and the eval runner records a failure with empty evidence before the expected-output contract can be satisfied. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to these observability evals.
